pack.name: font-fixtures
pack.summary: Real TTF, OTF, TTC, WOFF and WOFF2 binaries — the same faces in every wrapper, so a decoder can be checked against the sfnt each wrapper was built from.

license.covers: SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright 2010-2023 Adobe, with Reserved Font Name 'Source'. Permits use, study, modification and redistribution, including with software, and permits sale as part of a larger package. Two conditions shape how it may travel: the fonts may not be sold on their own, and a modified version may not carry the reserved name.

SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright 2020 The JetBrains Mono Project Authors, with Reserved Font Name 'JetBrains Mono'. Same terms as Adobe's: redistributable and sellable with software, not sellable alone, reserved name not reusable.

googlefonts/fontations is offered under Apache-2.0 or MIT at the reader's choice; the Apache grant is the one relied on here and the one snapshotted. Its test data mixes fonts the project built with subsets of third-party families carrying OFL-1.1 or Apache-2.0 upstream, none of it separately declared.

web-platform-tests is dual-licensed under the 3-Clause BSD License and the W3C 3-clause BSD License at the recipient's option; the BSD grant is the one relied on. Ahem, the CanvasTest metric fonts, the pass/fail pair and the MATH set were built for the suite. The root directory also holds vendored copies of Lato, Gentium Plus, Scheherazade, M+ 1p and others whose own upstreams are OFL-1.1 and which wpt does not separately declare — the repository-wide scope recorded here is the honest description of that.

SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright (c) 2003-2008 SIL International, with Reserved Font Names 'Gentium' and 'SIL'. Per the directory's README these are modified Gentium Basic: a four-face family for bold/italic selection and an ASCII-subsetted variant, differing mostly in name table and character map — which is what makes them useful for testing font matching rather than rendering.

SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright (c) 2013 Adobe Systems Incorporated, with Reserved Font Names 'CSS Half-Width Orientation Test' and 'CSS Full-Width Orientation Test'. Purpose-built OpenType fonts for testing vertical-writing orientation.

SIL Open Font License 1.1 over Noto subsets: CJK with and without `chws` spacing tables, Korean, Adlam, Cypriot, and a colour-emoji subset. Five subdirectories each carry their own copy of the OFL text and each is included in place beside its fonts; the snapshot in LICENSES/ is the CJK one, and they are identical in terms.

SIL Open Font License 1.1. A monospace Arabic webfont, present because it exercises bidi against line breaking and not every platform ships one — which makes it the font counterpart to what text-conformance-fixtures tests as character data.
SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright (c) 2026 Sajid Anwar. A font for validating baseline alignment, whose README documents the metrics each baseline is set to.
MIT, Copyright (c) 2017 Just van Rossum and contributors. These are fontTools' own regression fonts, several of them purpose-built minimal cases.

MIT, Copyright (c) 2019-2024 Rob Hagemans, over monobit and its test corpus. The corpus includes long-circulated bitmap faces (Computer Modern, System Fixed, Hershey vectors) gathered as conversion regression material and not separately declared.
